title: Uber Poised for In-Line Quarterly Gross Bookings, With Focus on AV Strategy, BofA Says

Uber Technologies' (UBER) third-quarter gross bookings are likely to meet Wall Street's expectations, with investors focused on the company's autonomous vehicle strategy and supply roadmap amid growing competition, BofA Securities said Wednesday.

The brokerage expects the ride-hailing giant to post gross bookings of about $59.78 billion when it reports September quarter results Nov. 4. The Street is looking for $59.77 billion, BofA said. The brokerage projects non-GAAP earnings at $0.91 a share versus the Street's $0.87 projection.

The company's shares were down 1% in Wednesday late-afternoon trade and have fallen 20% so far this year.

Uber's recent underperformance relative to the S&P 500 likely reflects AV concerns and high uncertainty on potential gas price impact to supply and volumes, as well as Walmart's (WMT) expansion into restaurant delivery, among other factors, BofA analyst Justin Post said in a note to clients.

Potential AV competition in the US, including from Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) Waymo unit and Tesla's (TSLA) Cybercab vehicle ramps, also weighed on Uber's share performance in the third quarter, Post said. "US supply roadmap will be the most important topic of the (third-quarter) call."

The brokerage reiterated its buy rating on the Uber stock, with a $101 price objective.

For the ongoing quarter, BofA lowered its gross bookings outlook for the company to $64.55 billion from $65.13 billion and its non-GAAP EPS expectations to $0.99 from $1.01.

"Buybacks and cost actions could support (fourth-quarter) EPS, while elevated gas prices could be a modest margin risk," Post said. "We expect healthy 27%, (adjusted) EPS growth in 2027."

Last month, Uber said it was cutting its workforce by about 10% as part of restructuring efforts aimed at removing management layers and reducing "complexity" across the business.

Earlier this month, the company agreed to acquire US-based catering platform ezCater in a $2.3 billion cash deal, as the ride-hailing giant looks to expand its food delivery business to more corporate customers.

DoorDash's (DASH) third-quarter results are slated to be released Nov. 4, while Lyft (LYFT) will report Nov. 5.

Walmart Inc. WMT and MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI are strengthening their competitive positions through digital innovation, expanding customer engagement and investments in their respective ecosystems. With evolving consumer preferences, technological advancements and profitability trends shaping their growth trajectories, a closer assessment of their fundamentals, earnings expectations and valuations can help identify the more promising investment opportunity.

Walmart, with a market cap of around $949.6 billion, is a global omnichannel retail giant with an extensive store network and a growing digital ecosystem spanning e-commerce, advertising, marketplace, membership and fulfillment services. Its scale, price leadership and expanding higher-margin businesses support its long-term growth prospects.

MercadoLibre is a leading e-commerce and fintech platform in Latin America, operating an integrated ecosystem across online commerce, payments, credit, advertising and financial services. Its expanding logistics infrastructure, Mercado Pago adoption and technology-driven initiatives provide multiple avenues for growth. The company currently has a market cap of $85.2 billion.

The Case for Walmart

Walmart's growth prospects are supported by its extensive retail network, competitive pricing and strengthening omnichannel capabilities. Its broad merchandise assortment and focus on affordability continue to attract shoppers across income groups, supporting customer traffic and market share gains. The company's vast store footprint also provides a strategic fulfillment advantage, enabling faster deliveries and greater shopping convenience.

Digital transformation remains a key growth catalyst. Walmart continues to benefit from growing e-commerce penetration, marketplace expansion and improved fulfillment capabilities. Faster delivery services are encouraging repeat purchases and strengthening customer engagement, supporting Walmart+ membership adoption. The company's ability to leverage stores for online order fulfillment also provides opportunities to improve delivery economics.

Its evolving business mix is another upside. Higher-margin revenue streams, including advertising, membership, marketplace services and data solutions, are becoming increasingly important contributors. These businesses, alongside supply-chain automation and improving delivery efficiency, are supporting e-commerce profitability. Walmart is also extending its digital platforms and membership offerings across international markets, creating additional opportunities for operational efficiencies and scalability.

Nevertheless, pharmacy-related deflation, rising healthcare and claims costs, higher depreciation expenses and continued investments in pricing and customer experience remain concerns. These factors could constrain near-term margin expansion. Despite such challenges, Walmart's resilient retail operations, growing digital ecosystem and improving business mix remain encouraging. Management's raised fiscal 2027 outlook on its second-quarter earnings call further reinforces confidence in its growth trajectory.

Investors interested in stocks from the Retail - Supermarkets sector have probably already heard of Tesco PLC (TSCDY) and Walmart (WMT). But which of these two stocks is more attractive to value investors? We'll need to take a closer look to find out.

Everyone has their own methods for finding great value opportunities, but our model includes pairing an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system with a strong Zacks Rank. The Zacks Rank is a proven strategy that targets companies with positive earnings estimate revision trends, while our Style Scores work to grade companies based on specific traits.

Tesco PLC and Walmart are sporting Zacks Ranks of #2 (Buy) and #3 (Hold), respectively, right now. The Zacks Rank favors stocks that have recently seen positive revisions to their earnings estimates, so investors should rest assured that TSCDY has an improving earnings outlook. However, value investors will care about much more than just this.

Value investors also try to analyze a wide range of traditional figures and metrics to help determine whether a company is undervalued at its current share price levels.

Our Value category grades stocks based on a number of key metrics, including the tried-and-true P/E ratio, the P/S ratio, earnings yield, and cash flow per share, as well as a variety of other fundamentals that value investors frequently use.

TSCDY currently has a forward P/E ratio of 16.89, while WMT has a forward P/E of 41.50. We also note that TSCDY has a PEG ratio of 1.91. This popular figure is similar to the widely-used P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also considers a company's expected EPS growth rate. WMT currently has a PEG ratio of 4.31.

Another notable valuation metric for TSCDY is its P/B ratio of 2.98. Investors use the P/B ratio to look at a stock's market value versus its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, WMT has a P/B of 9.06.

These metrics, and several others, help TSCDY earn a Value grade of A, while WMT has been given a Value grade of D.

TSCDY has seen stronger estimate revision activity and sports more attractive valuation metrics than WMT, so it seems like value investors will conclude that TSCDY is the superior option right now.

Investors pay 22.3 times earnings for Home Depot (HD) stock. That valuation is higher than for its closest rival, Lowe's, or for Amazon, but lower than for Walmart or Costco. Among these five large retailers, Home Depot retains the highest share of its sales as operating profit, yet it recorded the slowest sales growth over each company's latest four quarters. So how much extra are you paying for Home Depot's margin?

Home Depot Costs A Third More Than Lowe's

As the only other home improvement retailer in the group, Lowe's trades at 16.7 times earnings. This means a dollar of Home Depot's profit costs investors about a third more. That premium buys a wider margin: Home Depot recorded a 12.4% operating margin over its latest four quarters, compared with 11.4% at Lowe's. It does not buy faster growth. Lowe's increased its sales by 8.2% over its own latest four quarters, while Home Depot saw sales rise 2.5%.

Both home improvement stocks lost ground in the year to October 27, 2026. Home Depot fell 15.3% including dividends and Lowe's dropped 16.6%, while Amazon, Walmart and Costco all posted gains. Walmart and Costco cost more than Home Depot and grew faster, but both operate as consumer staples retailers with operating margins of 4.4% and 3.9%. Amazon, a broadline retailer, trades at a lower multiple of earnings and grew faster, with a margin only slightly thinner. But its $135 billion of net income ran above its $93.7 billion operating profit, so on operating profit alone it costs more than Home Depot.

Is Home Depot's Margin Its Thinnest In A Decade?

On a twelve-month basis, it is. Over the four quarters to August 2, 2026, Home Depot reported its lowest operating margin at any quarter end in the past ten years, falling from a high of 15.3%.

The latest quarter benefited from tariff refunds. Home Depot booked $685 million of refunds against the cost of products it had already sold, which management said added about 145 basis points to gross margin. Rising fuel, energy and input costs, alongside a product mix shift toward GMS and Mingledorff's, two businesses Home Depot bought, took most of that back, management said. Even with that benefit, the quarter's operating margin was 14.3%, down from 14.5% a year earlier.

Is ASO a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Academy Sports and Outdoors, Inc. on r/Valueinvesting by u/Embarrassed_Mix7664. Since the thesis was published on August 28th, ASO shares have gained 36.39%, supported by stronger earnings and a higher full-year profit outlook. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ASO. Academy Sports and Outdoors, Inc.'s share was trading at $59.33 as of October 27th 2026. ASO's trailing and forward P/E were 10.00 and 8.46 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a sporting goods retailer pitched as a great investment. ASO shares gained 21.48% over the last 12 months. Other retail stocks like Target and Walmart gained 57.26% and 16.46%, respectively, during the same period. Why are retail stocks rising, and does ASO still offer a compelling buying opportunity after its gains?

Is Fitness Champs (FCHL) One of the Worst Performing NASDAQ Stocks So Far in 2026?

Pixabay/Public Domain

In September, we published an article about Academy Sports (ASO) Rockets 14% on Solid Q2 Despite Consumer Spending Tests, highlighting an earnings report that sent shares sharply higher. But stronger results haven't erased Wall Street's caution. This article explains why analysts raised their price targets on ASO while keeping their ratings unchanged. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Academy Sports and Outdoors, Inc. (NASDAQ:ASO) is a value-focused sporting goods and outdoor retailer with a strong footprint across Texas and the Southeast. About a third of its sales come from outdoor, hunting and fishing gear, and roughly a fifth to a quarter of its products are private-label, giving it more control over pricing and margins. The bullish argument is that investors may be mistaking a return to normal after the pandemic boom for a permanent decline in the business.

That view got support in the first quarter, when comparable sales grew 2.9%, with both shopper traffic and average spending moving higher. The stock trades around $42, down about 31% from its February high of $62.45, and works out to only about 6.5 times the midpoint of management's full-year earnings guidance of $6.35 to $6.85 per share. That low multiple suggests the market is treating Academy Sports and Outdoors, Inc. like a retailer in structural trouble, even though its post-pandemic reset may already be behind it.

The case for that view rests on the idea that the company's three years of falling comparable sales were less about losing customers and more the natural comedown from an unusually high pandemic-era base. Revenue climbed from about $4.8 billion in fiscal 2019 to roughly $6.8 billion at the pandemic peak, before settling near $6.1 billion in fiscal 2025. Through that whole period, gross margin held steady around 34%, actually higher than the 29%-30% range it ran at before COVID. The first-quarter comparable sales growth of 2.9% looked encouraging next to peers: Dick's Sporting Goods, Inc. grew 4.9%, Target Corporation posted 3.8%, and Walmart Inc. came in at 2.6%. Wall Street, by contrast, reportedly expects Academy Sports and Outdoors, Inc. to grow only around 1% this quarter, a much lower bar than its larger competitors already cleared.

Beyond its stores, Walmart (WMT) earns from advertising, memberships, and its online marketplace, and stock buyers may be paying for those businesses. You probably think of Walmart as a discount store that keeps a few cents of each sales dollar as profit, and it still does. Yet the stock trades at 43.0 times earnings, against 22.6 for the S&P 500, and that is the contradiction. So how much of Walmart's profit growth do those three businesses drive?

Ads, Memberships, Marketplace: Almost Half Of Walmart's Profit Growth

During the August 20, 2026 call for fiscal Q2 2027, management said almost half of Walmart's profit growth came from areas like membership, advertising and marketplace. The company expects this to continue. Those businesses are growing far faster than Walmart as a whole. Global advertising, driven partly by Walmart Connect in the U.S., grew 38% in fiscal Q2 2027, while enterprise net sales grew 5% in constant currency. Membership income rose nearly 17%, and U.S. net sales from marketplace and fulfillment services climbed 52%.

Walmart's online sales are also getting more profitable, a shift management credits in part to strong ad and membership revenue. Its U.S. e-commerce business earned double-digit incremental margins in the first half of fiscal 2027, meaning each extra dollar of online sales added at least ten cents of profit.

What Should Worry A Walmart Buyer Now?

The concern lies with Walmart's stores. In-store comparable sales fell by a low single-digit percentage in fiscal Q2 2027, continuing a trend that began late in the prior fiscal year, management said. Management tied the drop mainly to lower health and wellness sales, most of which happen in store. Management also expects more than $2 billion of extra fuel costs in fiscal 2027, and sees more pressure on consumers than at the start of the year.

Yet management raised its full-year earnings guide to $2.80 to $2.87 a share, from $2.75 to $2.85. During the call, management pointed to growth in membership, advertising and fulfillment services as elements making the business more durable, adding that it expects profit to keep growing much faster than sales in 2027 and later years. The company's full-year guide already has operating income growing 7% to 8.5%, against sales growth of 4% to 5%.

Part of the fiscal 2027 lift came from outside the business, however. Walmart has received substantially all of about $2.9 billion in tariff refunds, which management said added about 750 basis points to adjusted operating income growth of over 17% in fiscal Q2 2027. Without those refunds, growth landed at the top end of management's 7% to 10% guide for the quarter.
